engines.why: vLLM's OpenAI-compatible server, 'vllm serve'. It is the default, and the only engine whose profiles carry tuned flags, so its capabilities turn on the memory fit, KV cache sizing, model-card flags, parser validation and the hardware definitions' forbidden flags.

install.any: uv venv ~/venvs/vllm && uv pip install vllm

engines.why: mlx-lm's OpenAI-compatible server, mlx_lm.server, which runs on the Apple Silicon GPU through MLX. It reads its tool-call and reasoning formats from the model's tokenizer, so a profile needs no parser flags. It has no API key and binds 127.0.0.1 by default, so the command leaves the host alone: listening beyond this machine is a choice to make in EXTRA_ARGS, knowing the endpoint is then open.

install.any: uv venv ~/venvs/mlx && uv pip install mlx-lm

engines.why: llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible server, llama-server. It serves GGUF on Metal, CUDA or the CPU, and sizes its own context and GPU layers to fit the machine, so a profile needs only the model. MODEL is passed as --alias too, so /v1/models reports exactly MODEL whether the model comes from the Hub or a file. It checks an API key, which it reads from LLAMA_API_KEY so the key is on no command line; with one set it binds every interface, and without one it stays on 127.0.0.1. It downloads a repo's GGUF itself, and its /health answers 200 only once the model is loaded.

TensorFold's OpenAI-compatible server, 'tensorfold serve', run from a recipe's image across the nodes of a cluster. Every rank runs the same command against the checkpoint's local snapshot, and rank 0 also takes the served name, host and port, which is what answers the API. It reads only the Hugging Face cache mounted from each node (HF_HUB_OFFLINE in the recipe), so the pinned models must be downloaded on every node before a launch, and a launch checks they are. Compiled kernels are kept per image patch set, since a kernel built for one set does not fit another, and the spill directory holds kept prompt states across restarts. It checks no API key: its host defaults to 127.0.0.1, and listening wider means fronting it with a proxy that checks one. /v1/models answers only once the model is loaded, which is what upstream's launcher waits for too.

params.name: tensor_parallel
params.why: --tp: how many GPUs the model is split over, across every node. One GPU a node, as on a DGX Spark, makes it the node count.

params.name: bind_host
params.why: --host on rank 0. TensorFold checks no API key, so the default keeps the endpoint on loopback; set it wider only behind a proxy that checks one.

params.name: kernel_cache
params.why: The host directory, under home, mounted at /cache for compiled CUDA kernels. A recipe names one per image patch set, so a different image never loads kernels built for another.

params.name: spill_dir
params.why: The host directory, under home, mounted at /spill, where --snapshot-dir /spill keeps prompt states on disk across restarts.
